title: Jersey City cost-of-living rent increase notice procedure
requirement: A landlord seeking a cost-of-living rent increase must give the tenant written notice at least 30 days before it takes effect, stating the CPI and other calculations, the allowable percentage under §260-3, and the tenant's right to contest within six months.
coverage_conditions: Landlords seeking cost-of-living increases on dwellings covered by the Jersey City Rent Control chapter.
quoted_span: Any landlord seeking a cost-of-living rental increase shall notify the tenant in writing at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the increase as required by law of the calculations involved in computing the increase

title: Jersey City capital improvement and service charge surcharge
requirement: A landlord must get Rent Leveling Board approval before imposing a capital improvement or service surcharge, and a capital improvement increase may not exceed 15% of the legal rent in the first year.
key_value: 15% of legal rent for the first year; depreciation max 10 years (major) / 5 years (minor)
coverage_conditions: Landlords seeking service or capital improvement surcharges on dwellings covered by the Jersey City Rent Control chapter.
exemptions: Emergency major capital improvements need no prior Board approval; only one major capital improvement increase per 12-month period, except emergency improvements.
quoted_span: A capital improvement increase resulting hereunder shall not exceed 15% of the legal rent for the first year of such increase.

title: Jersey City exemptions for new dwellings and dwellings vacant as of July 1, 1998
requirement: The chapter's rent limits do not apply to a new dwelling constructed between June 25, 1987 and June 25, 1992 (not for senior citizens) for up to the mortgage amortization period or 30 years, whichever is less, if the owner met the state filing requirements.
key_value: 30 years or mortgage amortization, whichever is less
coverage_conditions: Newly constructed dwellings and newly constructed housing space rented for the first time; dwellings certified vacant as of July 1, 1998.

conditions.text: dwellings certified by the Division of Tenant/Landlord Relations as vacant as of July 1, 1998 are permanently exempt

applicability.per_tenancy: The initial rent for newly constructed housing space rented for the first time is not restricted.
coverage_quotes: the provisions of this chapter shall not apply to a new dwelling which is constructed between June 25, 1987, through June 25, 1992, and which is not constructed for occupation by senior citizens, for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less

exemptions: New dwellings constructed between June 25, 1987 and June 25, 1992 (not for senior citizens) for up to 30 years or the mortgage amortization period, whichever is less; dwellings certified vacant as of July 1, 1998.
quoted_span: the provisions of this chapter shall not apply to a new dwelling which is constructed between June 25, 1987, through June 25, 1992, and which is not constructed for occupation by senior citizens, for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less
interaction: Applies in accordance with the state new-construction exemption in N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq.

title: Jersey City hardship rental increase
requirement: A landlord who cannot meet mortgage or operating expenses or does not make a fair return may apply to the Rent Leveling Board for a hardship increase after owning the building at least nine months; no increase may be imposed without Board approval.
coverage_conditions: Landlords of dwellings covered by the Jersey City Rent Control chapter who have owned the building at least nine months.
quoted_span: In the event that a landlord cannot meet his or her mortgage payments or operating expenses or does not make a fair return on his or her investment, he or she may apply to the Rent Leveling Board for increased rentals, provided that he or she has owned the building for at least nine months prior to the time he or she applies for an increase.
